My work sits at the intersection of research, program evaluation, and the use of evidence to improve services. I am especially interested in helping organizations ask useful questions, measure outcomes thoughtfully, and communicate findings in ways that support decisions.

## Research and evaluation

I serve as Director of Research and Evaluation at Didi Hirsch Mental Health Services, where I lead research, evaluation, and analytics supporting community mental health and related behavioral health programs. My work includes outcome measurement, assessment implementation, service evaluation, data quality, reproducible analyses, and communication of findings to clinical and organizational stakeholders.

I am interested in the practical challenges of moving from data to useful insight: how measures are defined, whose experiences are represented, what conclusions a research design supports, and how findings can inform improvements in care and organizational practice.

## Education and quantitative methods

I earned an **M.A. in Psychology with an emphasis in Quantitative Methods** from California State University, Fullerton, and a **B.A. in Psychology** with a minor in Philosophy from California State University, Dominguez Hills.

My training and research interests include psychological measurement, psychometrics, research methodology, statistical modeling, and applied data analysis.

## Teaching and mentorship

Alongside my research leadership responsibilities, I have provided research and program evaluation instruction and mentorship within an APA-accredited doctoral psychology internship program since 2016. I guide interns through applied research projects with an emphasis on research design, measurement, analysis, interpretation, and written and oral communication.

I am currently developing introductory statistics teaching resources that support conceptual understanding through guided practice and interactive demonstrations.

My scholarly work addresses community mental health service delivery, workforce experiences, treatment engagement, and program evaluation.
